SMTO-GML-0034 — Gmail isn't available on this SMTO server

GUID: a9aa83a1-b179-4eb9-a203-8e6f1df24ece
Slug: gmail-integration-unavailable
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use Gmail because the Gmail feature isn't switched on for this server. Your request never reached Gmail, so nothing in your mailbox changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, asking them to turn Gmail on for this server. Gmail is switched on in the server's own setup, which can't be changed from the conversation.
  2. Once they confirm Gmail is on, select More options › Parameter Store and check that your Gmail account is still listed. If the server's Parameter Store was also switched off, SMTO can't see your saved Gmail accounts, so check they are still there.
  3. Ask SMTO again in the conversation, naming your account, for example 'Use @work_gmail to list today's unread mail'. Your earlier request was stopped before reaching Gmail, so asking again is safe once Gmail is on.

What success looks like

  • SMTO answers your Gmail request with results instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • If Gmail is on and the error continues, send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO again. Don't delete your saved Gmail account to try to fix this; it holds your connection.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • No enabled Gmail service was available for the request: the Server's Gmail service was not created (for example because the Parameter Store is disabled) or AOR_GMAIL_ENABLED is false.

What this means

  • Gmail API/capability lookup finds no service instance or a service whose enabled flag is false. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Gmail API/capability lookup finds no service instance or a service whose enabled flag is false.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish deliberate integration disablement from absent service wiring.

How to fix it

  • The Gmail routes return 503 and gmail.* tools fail when the Gmail service is missing or its enabled flag is false. Set AOR_GMAIL_ENABLED=true and AOR_AGENT_PARAMETER_STORE_ENABLED=true (both default to true) in the Server environment, restart the Server, and confirm the effective values on the Runtime page under Integrations and automation. Do not remove saved Gmail accounts while diagnosing.
  • Restore the enabled Gmail integration and its Parameter Store configuration before using Gmail actions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended Gmail service and its required account configuration are available.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
